//: Tiny Tapeout default configuration plus the IHP SRAM macro RM_IHPSG13_1P_64x16_c2 as each engine's program store.
Macro recipe: Ken Pettit's walkthrough (kdp1965/ihp-um-janestreet-prism) and J.L. Nuijens's config (JLNuijens/ttihp-cpu-1-1-uart).
The tile's Metal4 stripes are run across the macros by Project.ExtendPowerStripes (librelane_plugin_sram_pdn.py at the
repo root, odb_stripes.py), replacing the flow's GeneratePDN; pdn_cfg.tcl is LibreLane's without the per-macro grid.
40 MHz: a 10 Mbit Manchester half-bit is then exactly two clocks.
pnr.sdc is LibreLane's base.sdc with the hold clock uncertainty at 0.1 ns (setup stays 0.25 ns).
USE_SRAM selects the macro in prog_mem.v and fifo_mem.v (flip-flops are the default build of the design repository).
Magic DRC off and KLayout DRC on: Magic reads the macro from its LEF abstract and reports overlaps at the VDD!/VDDARRAY! break that are not in the GDS.
Stripe grid on the macro's supply columns: VDD!/VSS! alternate every 5.62 um (2.1 + 3.52), VDD! to VDD! 11.24 um, 4 x 11.24 = 44.96.
Core x origin is 2.88 (6 sites), so stripes sit at 9.03 + 44.96 k; a macro at x = 3.36 + 44.96 k has its first VDD! column (5.665 in) on one.
Three program-store macros (236.80 x 64.36 um) along the bottom edge, FS so their Metal2 signal pins face the core; x on the 44.96 grid (k = 0, 6, 12).
Engine 0's TX FIFO macro above engine 0's program store (same x, same stripe columns), FS, at y 98.28: a 30.14 um channel above the lower macro's pin face (y 68.14).

Routing kept off the macro footprints on the tile's routing layers: bottom row from the die edge (y 0, so no wire runs under a macro) and 2 um past each side, stopping 2.6 um short of the pin face at the top (y 68.14); the FIFO macro from 0.48 um below its bottom (the vertical halo, y 97.80) to 2.6 um short of its pin face (y 162.64).

Timing repair as kdp1965/ihp-um-janestreet-prism: the macro's clock-to-data is about 5.3 ns at the slow corner, so the instruction fan-out must be buffered with strong cells and repaired again on routed parasitics.
